html:
Malabar is the northern half of Kerala's coast, around Calicut, today's Kozhikode. On the 1783 and 1800 maps it is passing from Mysore's rule to Britain's.

For centuries Malabar was the world's main source of black pepper, and its ports drew Arab, Chinese and later European ships. The Zamorin of Calicut was its leading ruler, and Vasco da Gama landed near Calicut in 1498. The Mappila Muslims, descended in part from Arab traders, were a large part of its people.

In 1766 Hyder Ali of Mysore conquered Malabar, and his son Tipu Sultan held it until his defeat. By the Treaty of Seringapatam in 1792, Tipu gave it to the British, who made it a district of the Madras Presidency. To the south lay Cochin.
sum: Malabar is the northern half of Kerala's coast, around Calicut, today's Kozhikode. On the 1783 and 1800 maps it is passing from Mysore's rule to Britain's.
